name: Lime
imageAlt: fresh whole green lime and a half slice on a reflective dark surface with water droplets
description: Lime (Citrus aurantiifolia) is a highly acidic, energetically vibrant citrus fruit functioning as a premier organic fluid optimizer. The core therapeutic value of the lime resides in its complex organic acid matrix, heavily dominated by exogenous citric acid, alongside an elite payload of L-ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) and volatile monoterpenes like d-limonene. Operating within cellular systems, these bioactive substrates optimize non-heme iron absorption, neutralize heavy free radicals, and act as significant dietary alkalizing agents once fully metabolized via the citric acid cycle.
macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, raw flesh without peel)
macroIntro: Lime flesh presents an ultra-low-calorie, hydration-centric macronutrient architecture with minimal simple sugars and a functional matrix of soluble pectin fibers.
microIntro: The cellular vacuoles of lime juice house a highly bioavailable reservoir of radical-scavenging antioxidants, mineral chelators, and essential extracellular electrolytes.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates

microNutrients.name: Citric Acid

microNutrients.name: Flavonoids (Hesperidin)

microNutrients.name: Potassium

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
microNutrients.description: An essential water-soluble coenzyme building block required for managing regular nucleic acid synthesis and regulating cellular replication loops.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: Supports bone health and crucial intracellular signaling pathways.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Essential cofactor for over 300 enzymatic reactions, including energy production.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
microNutrients.description: Supports neurotransmitter production and metabolic health.

healthBenefits: Collagen Synthesis Acceleration: Concentrated Vitamin C acts as an absolute structural cofactor for prolyl hydroxylase enzymes, directly assembling tough human dermal and vascular collagen frameworks.
Systemic Non-Heme Iron Chelation: Abundant native citric acid and ascorbic complexes reduce non-heme dietary iron into highly absorbable ferrous configurations within the intestinal lumen.
Urolithiasis Prevention: Elevated dietary citrate complexes bind tightly to urinary calcium channels, effectively inhibiting the crystallization and growth of calcium oxalate kidney stones.
Vascular Capillary Reinforcement: Active bioflavonoid profiles reduce vascular permeability, improving capillary wall strength and maintaining systemic microcirculation parameters.
Endogenous Salivary Activation: The sharp, low-pH organic acid matrix stimulates immediate salivary and gastric juice cascades, drastically improving protein digestion loops.
precautionsIntro: Dental Enamel Acid Dissolution, Phytophotodermatitis Risks, and Gastric Mucosal Irritations: Strategic consumption protects structural barrier systems.
precautions: Dental Enamel Demineralization: The high concentration of raw citric acid gives lime juice a very low pH (~2.0). Direct, frequent exposure can chemically dissolve protective hydroxyapatite crystals in tooth enamel, inducing permanent sensitivity. Rinsing the mouth with pure water immediately after ingestion is advised.

Furanocoumarin Mediated Phytophotodermatitis: Lime peel containing volatile essential oils is rich in furanocoumarins. If skin surfaces are contaminated with lime oil and subsequently exposed to Ultraviolet (UV) solar radiation, a intense photochemical reaction can cause severe blistering, hyperpigmentation, and burns.

Acute Gastric Mucosal Irritation: In individuals presenting with active hyperacidic gastritis, peptic ulcer diseases, or severe gastroesophageal reflux (GERD), the direct entry of concentrated lime acid can sharply irritate hypersensitive mucosal walls, triggering acute heartburn and esophageal spasms.
